subject: Keystone Labs - Solution acceptance & interop validation check-in
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Summers <ellie.summers@keystonelabs.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Keystone Labs - kickoff for solution acceptance / validation

Hi Ellie —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, Keystone’s integration with Redwood Dedicated will be part of our standard partner technical acceptance before we enable a marketplace listing. I attached a first-draft architecture diagram and a short validation checklist so we can align on scope.

High-level ask for the run-through:
- Confirm networking (VPC peering vs. PrivateLink) and egress controls
- Validate model variant/quantization strategy for your inference workloads
- Smoke test prefix cache and batching behavior with a 95th %-ile latency SLO
- Confirm logging/audit access patterns for SOC-2 evidence requests

Suggested times this week: Thu 10/29 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 10/30 14:00–15:00 PT. If those don't work, propose alternatives.

Attachments: keystone-arch-diagram-v1.pdf, redwood-validation-checklist.xlsx

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Partner Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0172

Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Keystone Labs - kickoff for solution acceptance / validation

Marissa —

Thanks for the doc. Thu 10/29 10:00 PT works for our infra and ML engineering leads. I'll loop in Tomás (network) and attach our current network topology image.

Quick answers up front:
- We're planning PrivateLink for the initial prod integration; VPC peering is an option but we'd prefer managed endpoints for auditability.
- For models, our baseline is FP16 on A10G; we'll aim to try an INT8 quantized build if Redwood's runtime supports it in the Dedicated tier.

Attaching: keystone-network-topology.png

Ellie
Ellie Summers | Head of Integrations, Keystone Labs
ellie.summers@keystonelabs.com | +1 646-555-2045

Subject: Agenda + validation checklist for Thu 10/29 run-through (10:00 PT)

Ellie / Tomás —

Confirming our call for Thu 10/29 10:00–11:00 PT. Agenda (30/30 split):
- 10:00–10:30 PT: Architecture and networking (Tomás + Sergio)
- 10:30–11:00 PT: Performance validation and runbook items (Karthik + Marissa)

I've exported the checklist to a workbook and pre-populated the items we'll attempt during the smoke tests. Notes in the doc include expected token throughput ranges, target 95p latency thresholds, and a simple load pattern we'll run from our Dedicated test pool.

Pre-call asks (helps shorten the session):
1) If you can share a short sample request pattern (payload sizes, avg tokens per request) that mirrors your prod usage, paste into the checklist.
2) Confirm whether your security team requires a managed endpoint or if service account keys are acceptable for test peering.

Attachments: redwood-validation-checklist.xlsx

See you on the call —
Marissa

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Tomás Vega <tomas.vega@keystonelabs.com>, Ellie Summers <ellie.summers@keystonelabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Agenda + validation checklist for Thu 10/29 run-through (10:00 PT)

Quick technical note following the architecture discussion this morning:
- For your conversational workload, keep an eye on KV cache retention across short-lived sessions; Redwood's Dedicated runtime will preserve KV cache per connection but we need to align TTLs if you use many ephemeral pods.
- On quantization: INT8 paths typically save 2.5–3x token cost, but we'll validate any quality delta on your prompt set. If the model variant you're using has fused attention kernels, we should test the 2k vs 8k sequence length profiles; performance characteristics differ.

I'll upload a short runbook fragment after I sync with infra; Karthik, please add any API-level test hooks you want enabled.

Sergio
Sergio Alvarez | Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Ellie Summers <ellie.summers@keystonelabs.com>

Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Agenda + validation checklist for Thu 10/29 run-through (10:00 PT)

Thanks for the session — good progress. Next items from our side:
- We attached a short sample traffic CSV into the shared Drive folder (see link). It averages 1.2k tokens/request and ~15 requests/minute during expected peak.
- Keystone infra prefers PrivateLink for prod peering; for the smoke tests we're fine with temporary managed endpoint credentials.
- On quantization: we ran a small INT8 pilot internally and saw negligible regressions on intent classification, but we'll share full evals this week.

One question: for SOC-2 evidence, which specific logs do you surface from the Dedicated control plane? We need examples to show our auditors.

Ellie

Subject: Next steps & artifacts to close validation (DocuSign + evidence)

Ellie / Tomás —

Thanks for the thorough follow-up and the sample traffic — that's super helpful. To close out the Partner Technical Acceptance we need the following by EOD Fri 11/05:
- Signed Partner addendum (I attached a DocuSign link below).
- A short export of your internal evaluation of the INT8 pilot (results + one sample prompt set)
- Confirmation on PrivateLink peering and the target environment (staging/prod)

Regarding SOC-2 evidence: Redwood Dedicated control plane exposes the following artifacts for audits:
- Per-request audit logs (timestamped, model id, truncated prompt hash)
- Admin access logs (who/when, IAM role changes)
- Configuration snapshots for each deployment (image + kernel config)

I've attached the refined validation checklist and included a stub for the runbook Sergio mentioned. Once we have the signed addendum I'll schedule a 2-hour run from our Dedicated test pool to exercise the smoke checks.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/sheets/abc123-keystone-nda
Drive (artifacts): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1Keystone-interop

Best —
